newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia won't print money to pay back wages - Yasin.
newsitem.headline: Russia won't print money to pay back wages - Yasin.

text.p: Russia will not print extra money to solve its acute problem of non-payments and wage arrears, Itar-Tass news agency quoted Economy Minster Yevgeny Yasin as saying on Thursday.
"It is not money supply we are having shortage of, but accessible loans," he told a cabinet meeting.
He said the government would preserve its policy of gradual money supply growth, running just ahead of inflation levels.
Statistics committee officials said Russia issued 19.38 trillion roubles in cash in January-November 1996, well below 35.35 trillion in the same period of 1995.

Yasin said he expected difficulties with payments of wages, pensions and social benefits to last through the first quarter of 1997 and said the situation would not change drastically for the better before the end of next year.
But he said the government would take short-term measures to help with payments of back wages and pensions.
Corporate debt and wage arrears are among Russia's biggest economic problems.
